title: Thousand Oaks Post Acute, LLC ranked No. 3 in Ventura County nursing home capacity in Q1
text:
Thousand Oaks Post Acute, LLC was identified as the third largest nursing home in Ventura County during the first quarter of 2026, data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) shows.
The facility offered 123 beds in total, surpassing the Ventura County average by 25 beds as of the same quarter. On average, 99.1 residents were cared for at the center each day.
The CMS awarded Thousand Oaks Post Acute, LLC a 3 out of 5 overall rating, trailing behind California’s nursing home average rating of 3.2.
For the same period, Shoreline Care Center was Ventura County’s largest nursing home with 193 beds, while Victoria Care Center followed with 188 beds.
By the end of the first quarter of 2026, Thousand Oaks Post Acute, LLC had incurred one fine totaling $20,703 and received one penalty.
Ventura County, California counted 17 for-profit nursing homes in total.
Estimates from the U.S. Census Bureau show that the population of older adults nationwide is rising as the younger population declines. Between 2020 and 2024, those age 65 and over increased by 13%, while the population under 18 declined by 1.7%. The country’s older adult demographic has sharply expanded in the last century, growing from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million by 2024.
A 2021 analysis found that about half of this age group, around 28 million people, could need long-term services and support, while projections indicate over one-third may eventually require care in a nursing home.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
